sections.h2: Selling a house in Delaware, Ohio
sections.html:
Agent, no agent, or cash buyer: in Delaware the paperwork lands in the same two county offices, the Auditor and the Recorder. The city is the county seat, on the Olentangy River beside U.S. Route 23, north of Columbus. People keep arriving. July 2025 shows 46,636 residents against 41,297 in 2020, a gain of 12.9 percent.

Demand has pushed prices up. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $318,400, and 64.7 percent of the 16,728 households own theirs. Renters pay a median $1,286 a month, and owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,892. The city pitches itself on affordability, lower income taxes and small town living. Houses around downtown and Ohio Wesleyan University are the oldest, so buyers there tend to ask about roofs, wiring and earlier repairs.

sections.h2: Which school district covers your address
sections.html:
Delaware City, Olentangy Local and Buckeye Valley all have territory inside the city limits, so two neighbors can sit in different districts. Many buyers shop by district first.

Delaware City is the historic city district, at about 6,000 students. Olentangy Local is much bigger, over 24,000, and stretches across several jurisdictions. Buckeye Valley, around 2,300 students, only partly reaches the city. Look the parcel up in county records, or ask the district, before a listing says which one applies. Naming the wrong district can cost you a buyer who picked the house for its schools.

A single city department runs zoning, property maintenance and building review, and its building division is state-certified. Its FAQ covers the questions sellers and buyers tend to raise.

  • Fences, decks, sheds, garages and additions need permits, as does structural, electrical or mechanical work. Patios don't.
  • Boundary disagreements between neighbors are civil matters. The city recommends a survey.
  • Contractors no longer register with the city as of 2026.
  • Every vehicle, trailers included, parks on a hard surface: asphalt, concrete or existing gravel. Adding or widening gravel parking is prohibited.
  • Code enforcement pulls signs from the right-of-way, tree lawns and utility poles.

Built a deck or shed without a permit? Call the Building Division and ask how to legalize it before a buyer's inspector spots it.

Notices are posted at the property. When the house is vacant, the notice also goes by mail to whoever the county auditor lists as owner. If the deadline lapses, the city can do the work and send you the bill. A bill left unpaid may become a lien or be added to your tax bill, and the city prosecutor may file charges too.

Settle any notice before you list. Title searches turn up liens, and a lien can stall a closing or come out of your proceeds. Unsure whether a notice was ever issued? Ask code enforcement for the address history. Pay or repair what is open, keep the receipt, and carry it to closing so the title company can clear the item.

sections.h2: Valuation, deeds and recording in Delaware County
sections.html:
The Auditor's informal review for the 2026 triennial update is over. To dispute a valuation formally, file with the Board of Revision between January 1, 2027 and March 31, 2027, using the form the Auditor posts. That forms page also has the Real Property Conveyance Fee Statement, DTE 100, and the Auditor's staff can tell you the conveyance fee for your sale.

Delaware County Recorder, deed recording

County fee schedules change, so phone first if you plan to mail a check.

R.C. 5302.30 puts a duty on owners of homes with as many as four units: complete Ohio's disclosure form and give the buyer a signed copy. Should the buyer get it, or an amended version, only after a contract is signed, the buyer may cancel in writing for three business days. That right ends at whichever comes first, thirty days after acceptance or closing.

Sales, land installment contracts, lease-options and exchanges are all covered. Heirs who never lived in the inherited house for a year are excluded, as are transfers between spouses or to direct-line relatives. Complete the form when you list, so no late amendment hands the buyer an exit.

sections.h2: When a cash purchase helps a Delaware owner
sections.html:
Cash fits when speed or condition matters more than the top dollar. Postponed repairs, a code notice, tenants who won't leave or an estate that isn't settled can all drag out a listing. A buyer who takes the house as it stands skips the showings and the repair negotiation.

It also suits owners who already moved away. An empty house draws code attention, and notices go to the owner of record by mail, so a seller in another town can miss a deadline. A fast sale closes that exposure.

Before accepting a cash figure, set it against what a listing would net after repairs, months of carrying costs and tax that keeps accruing. Put each buyer's written price, closing date and cost split side by side.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before you list
sections.html:
Pull together the signed Ohio disclosure form, receipts for permitted work, any closed violation notices and your latest tax bill. If a homeowner association or a lease is involved, add those documents as well. Buyers and title companies ask for the same items, and having them ready shortens the days between contract and closing.

Also check your deed for the legal description and the exact owner names. A misspelled name or a missing co-owner signature is a small error that can send a deed back from the Recorder and push the closing date.

When you accept an offer, a title company searches the property record. Old city invoices that became liens, unpermitted structures and recording errors surface at this stage. Fix them before closing day, since the buyer's lender or attorney will insist on clear title.

At signing you execute the deed, the conveyance fee statement goes to the Auditor, and the Recorder files the deed at the fees shown above. Take photo identification and any payoff letters along. For an inherited house, add the paperwork that shows who holds title, because an unsettled estate is a frequent cause of stalled closings.

No lender in the middle means a cash buyer can often close sooner. The title search, the state form and the recording still happen, so ask early who pays for each.

faqs.q: What is the window to contest a Delaware County valuation?
faqs.a: Informal review for the 2026 triennial update has ended. Formal complaints to the Board of Revision run from January 1, 2027 to March 31, 2027, on the Auditor's form.

faqs.q: Which home projects need a Delaware permit?
faqs.a: Fences, decks, sheds, garages and additions, plus any structural, electrical or mechanical work. Patios are exempt. Before listing, ask the Building Division how to close out an unpermitted structure.

faqs.q: What if I ignore a Delaware violation notice?
faqs.a: The city may do the repair and bill you. An unpaid bill can become a lien or land on your tax bill, and the city prosecutor may file charges.

faqs.q: Where is the Delaware County Recorder and what are its deed fees?
faqs.a: At 145 N. Union Street in Delaware. A deed costs $39 for its first two pages, which includes a $5 preservation surcharge, then $8 for each page after.

faqs.q: How do I tell which district my Delaware home is in?
faqs.a: Delaware City, Olentangy Local and Buckeye Valley all reach into the city. Check the parcel in county records or ask the district before naming one.
